intro: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 and became famous for peace, democracy and nature conservation.

chapters.title: Stone spheres
text: Indigenous peoples carved hundreds of almost perfectly round stone spheres, some over 2 m wide, in the Diquís delta, a World Heritage site.

chapters.title: A quiet colony
text: Spain called it the 'rich coast', but found little gold. It was a poor, remote province of the Captaincy General of Guatemala. Costa Rica became independent in 1821.

chapters.title: No army
text: After a short civil war in 1948, José Figueres abolished the army and spent the money on schools and health. Costa Rica has been a stable democracy since. President Óscar Arias won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987 for helping end Central America's wars.

highlight.title: No army
highlight.text: Costa Rica is one of the few countries with no armed forces.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Pure life', a common Costa Rican saying.
Travel to enjoy and protect nature.
